messages:
marina: Heads up — ACME opened an escalation: big p95/p99 spike on the embeddings endpoint after last night's deploy. Customer saw timeouts + 500s, traced to retries. I see GPU allocation failures on nodes g-run-45/g-run-47.

chloe: Can you drop the error snippets and which model/variant?

marina: Model: text-embed-2-small-q (rolled v2 to 20% last night). Customer also started sending much longer histories. Errors: 
```
[2026-03-16 01:12:03] runtime: CUDA OOM trying to allocate 1.2GiB (total 14.7GiB)
[2026-03-16 01:12:03] runtime: allocation failed after 3 retries
[2026-03-16 01:12:03] runtime: KV cache growth: tenant=acme cache_bytes=1.9GiB -> eviction triggered
[2026-03-16 01:12:04] http: 500 internal server error, retries=2
```

raj: This looks like a combo of KV cache growth + fragmentation (small free spans but not contiguous). The OOMs + retries will push p95 up. Any change to batch size or concurrency?

marina: No explicit batch change for ACME. They did ramp request size (longer inputs). We do have continuous-batching enabled for the backend.

oliver: Immediate mitigations we should try:
1) Force tenant routing to a lower-memory variant (smaller model or CPU fallback)
2) Set per-tenant max_batch_size=1 and lower concurrency
3) Restart affected inference pods to reclaim fragmented GPU memory

Commands I'm running now:
```bash
# route tenant to smaller model variant
redwood route update --tenant acme --model text-embed-2-mini --weight 100
# restart pods on problematic nodes
kubectl get pods -l app=inf-runtime -o wide | grep g-run-45 | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -I{} kubectl delete pod {}
```

raj: Also flip on aggressive KV eviction and trigger allocator compaction: set KV_EVICTION_THRESHOLD=0.6 and REDWOOD_ALLOC_COMPACT=1 on the runtime env for the rollout. If fragmentation is severe, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 / jemalloc tuning helps.

marina: Applying the env changes to the canary now, setting per-tenant batch to 1 for ACME.

sophia: (ACME) We're seeing retries and cost spikes — any ETA for a stable fix?

oliver: Short term ETA ~30m for routing + restarts to take effect. Long term we need allocator tuning and a model sizing policy.

raj: Follow-ups for a durable solution:
- Open INF ticket to evaluate allocator config (jemalloc vs tcmalloc) and arena counts
- Add proactive KV cache watermark monitoring per-tenant (alert at 50% of per-host GPU memory)
- Consider automatic tenant throttling when KV growth + fragmented free memory observed
(I'm filing INF-8237 now)

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-345 assigned -> raj, oliver

chloe: After mitigation, capture: pmap (process GPU allocations), nvtop snapshot, and last 200 dmesg lines. Also collect runtime heap snapshots and KV cache sizes per-tenant.

marina: Adding pmap + dmesg excerpt from g-run-45 before restart: 
```
00000000:  6.1GiB mapped (nvml handles show multiple small allocations)
[   12.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[   12.346001] arr: failed allocate 1228800 bytes
```

marina: Rolling back the v2 rollout for ACME and routing to text-embed-2-mini. Will update customer post-verify. :thumbsup:

oliver: Good. After we stabilize, let's run a short A/B to compare KV growth between quantized and mini variants. If mini keeps mem pressure lower we should add an auto-fallback policy.

raj: One final note — if we see repeated fragmentation OOMs on the same hosts, we should mark them for a controlled reboot and replace with fresh instances. Long-lived fragmentation is low-cost to trigger but high-cost to mitigate at runtime.

marina: Logged progress; will post updates in 30m.
